Example Chart

Interactive examples and guidelines for Chart.js and Observable Plot data visualizations in InsightPage.

Example Chart

InsightPage supports rich interactive charts and data visualizations using Chart.js-style YAML syntaxes (chart) and Observable Plot (plot / observableplot).

Chart.js Style YAML Charts

Render interactive charts using unified YAML configurations across Bar, Line, Scatter, Pie / Donut / PolarArea, Radar, and Sankey charts.

Unified Chart Configuration Reference

All Chart DSL charts share a consistent set of configuration keys:

Category Options & Syntax Description Supported Chart Types
Chart Types type: bar | line | pie | donut (doughnut) | polararea | radar | sankey | scatter (point, scatterplot) Specify the visualization type to render. All Chart Types
Data Sourcing id: table-id / table: "#table-id"
data: path/to/file.csv
source: / file: / dataset:		 Bind directly to markdown tables (with or without # / ^ prefixes) or external CSV / TSV / JSON data files. All Chart Types
Mark Lines markLines: / markLine: / marks:
- { y: 80, label: "Target", style: dashed, color: "#10b981", strokeWidth: 1.5 }
- { x: 50, label: "Threshold", style: dotted }
- { x: "Q3", label: "Milestone" }		 Add horizontal (y:) or vertical (x:) reference threshold lines with labels and custom styling (solid, dashed, dotted). Supports both numeric and categorical coordinates. Bar, Line, Scatter
Scales & Log Scales xScale: log / yScale: log
xLog: true / yLog: true
scales: { x: { type: log }, y: { type: log } }		 Switch axis scale to logarithmic. Automatically suppresses 0-baseline collision on log scales. Bar, Line, Scatter
Domain & Min/Max xMin: 0 / xMax: 100
yMin: 0 / yMax: 500
xDomain: [0, 50] / yDomain: [100, 1000]		 Pin explicit bounds and intervals for X or Y axes. Bar, Line, Scatter
Axis Inversion & Visibility xReverse: true / yReverse: true
xDisplay: false / yDisplay: false		 Invert axis direction (e.g. rankings, depth) or toggle axis visibility for clean sparklines. Bar, Line, Scatter
Zero Baseline beginAtZero: true Ensure linear quantitative axes start at 0, preventing truncated baselines. Bar, Line, Scatter
Grid Controls grid: false
xGrid: true / yGrid: false		 Granularly enable or disable grid lines globally or independently per axis. Bar, Line, Scatter
Area Shading & Fill Opacity area: true / fill: true
fillOpacity: 0.35 / transparency: 0.2		 Turn line charts into shaded area charts with customizable fill opacity. Line
Data Values & Filtering showLabels: true / dataLabels: true
labelFilter: ["Target", "Peak"]
fontSize: 11		 Display direct numeric values, with support for selective label filtering and custom text size. Bar, Line, Scatter
Colors & Fills color: / fill: "#3b82f6"
colors: [...] / palette: [...]
colorScheme: / scheme: "tableau10" / "accent" / "set2" / "turbo"		 Customize palette with hex colors, array lists, or standard D3 categorical schemes. All Chart Types
Legend legend: true / legend: false Toggle legend display (automatically defaults based on series count or categorical/continuous color channel). All Chart Types
Title, Subtitle & Caption title: "Chart Title"
subtitle: "Additional context"
caption: "Figure 1. Source reference"		 Add informative chart titles, subtitles, and explanatory captions. All Chart Types
Container Width width: 80% / width: 600px / width: 500 Sets maximum container width for responsive presentation. All Chart Types
Scatter Trendlines trending: true
trendline: { stroke: "#6366f1", strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "4,4", grouped: true }		 Add linear regression trendlines. Supports log-space regression on logarithmic axes, custom styles, and per-series grouping (grouped: true / bySeries: true). Scatter
Scatter Fill & Bubble Size fill: <column> / color: <column>
r: <column|number> / size: <column|number>
colorScale: log / colorLog: true		 Map columns to point fill colors (continuous ramp or discrete swatches) and bubble radii for 4D scatter bubble charts. Scatter
Sankey Links & Flows links: / flows: / series: [{ data: [...] }]
Tuple: [source, value, target] or [source, target, value]
Object: { source, target, value }		 Configure multi-stage flow networks. Nodes are automatically derived or defined via nodes: [{ name }]. Supports custom node/link colors via colorFrom:, colorTo:, colors:, colorMode:, and custom vertical ordering via priority:. Sankey
Schema Mappings schemas: / schema: / mapping:
{ x, y, labels, series, fill, r }		 Map specific table or dataset columns to chart visual dimensions. All Chart Types
Adaptive Axis Ticks ticks: 6 / x: { ticks: 8, tickRotate: -45 }
y: { ticks: 5, tickFormat: "~s" }
tickRotate: -30 / tickSpacing: 40		 Automatically adapts tick density, stepping, and rotation to prevent label overlapping on dense or narrow axes. Supports explicit tick counts, custom rotation, spacing, and formatting. Bar, Line, Scatter

1. Bar Chart Example (with Mark Lines, Axis Labels & Value Labels)

  Test1 Test2 Test3
Data1 1 2 3.33
Data2 3 2 1
Data3 4.5 4 2

^table

type: bar
id: table
layout: rows
x: "Metrics"
y: "Score"
showLabels: true
markLines:
  - y: 3.0
    label: "Target Benchmark"
    style: dashed
    color: "#f59e0b"
width: 80%

2. Line Chart Example (with Mark Lines, Log Scale & Custom Palette)

type: line
x: "Quarter"
y: "Revenue ($K)"
yScale: log
showLabels: true
labels: ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"]
colorScheme: "tableau10"
series:
  - title: "2024 Revenue"
    data: [120, 190, 300, 500]
  - title: "2025 Target"
    data: [150, 230, 340, 580]
markLines:
  - y: 250
    label: "Break-even Milestone"
    style: dotted
    color: "#10b981"
width: 550px

2b. Shaded Area Chart Example (with Area Fill, Opacity, BeginAtZero & Selective Labels)

type: line
title: "Monthly Bandwidth Usage"
subtitle: "Network Ingress (GB)"
area: true
fillOpacity: 0.3
beginAtZero: true
dataLabels: ["May", "Jul"]
labels: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul"]
series:
  - title: "Ingress"
    data: [120, 150, 180, 220, 310, 290, 420]
markLines:
  - x: "May"
    label: "Capacity Upgrade"
    style: dashed
    color: "#6366f1"
width: 550px

4. Sankey Flow Diagram Example

InsightPage supports multiple Sankey data formats, including 3-element tuple arrays [source, value, target] and object flows { from, to, flow }. You can customize node positioning with priority: and link/node colors with colorFrom: and colorTo::

type: sankey
labels: ["Oil", "Natural Gas", "Coal", "Fossil Fuels", "Electricity", "Energy"]
series:
  - data:
      - ["Oil", 15, "Fossil Fuels"]
      - ["Natural Gas", 20, "Fossil Fuels"]
      - ["Coal", 25, "Fossil Fuels"]
      - ["Coal", 25, "Electricity"]
      - ["Fossil Fuels", 60, "Energy"]
      - ["Electricity", 25, "Energy"]
priority:
  Oil: 1
  Natural Gas: 2
  Coal: 3
  Fossil Fuels: 1
  Electricity: 2
  Energy: 1
colorFrom:
  Oil: "black"
  Coal: "gray"
  "Fossil Fuels": "slategray"
  Electricity: "blue"
  Energy: "orange"
colorTo:
  Oil: "black"
  Coal: "gray"
  "Fossil Fuels": "slategray"
  Electricity: "blue"
  Energy: "orange"
width: 650px

5. Radar Chart Example

Radar charts visualize multidimensional attributes across concentric web rings:

type: radar
labels: ["Speed", "Reliability", "Comfort", "Safety", "Efficiency"]
series:
  - title: "Model Alpha"
    data: [80, 90, 70, 85, 60]
  - title: "Model Beta"
    data: [60, 70, 90, 95, 80]
width: 450px

6. Scatter Chart Example

Render scatter point plots with trending regression lines, custom-styled mark lines, legends, and linear or logarithmic axes:

    style: dashed
    color: "#10b981"
  - x: 40
    label: "Midpoint Threshold"
    style: dotted
    color: "#f59e0b"
x:
  label: "Study Hours"
y:
  label: "Exam Score"
series:
  - title: "Cohort A"
    data:
      - [10, 35]
      - [18, 48]
      - [25, 62]
      - [32, 70]
      - [45, 88]
      - [50, 95]
  - title: "Cohort B"
    data:
      - [12, 28]
      - [20, 42]
      - [28, 55]
      - [38, 74]
      - [48, 82]
      - [55, 91]
width: 600px

7. External CSV / JSON Dataset Loading

InsightPage Chart DSL can load external dataset files directly without complex data-processing grammar, just like Timeline charts:

title: China Trade policy uncertainty
type: line
data: 5-Data/chinaEPU/China_Trade_policy_uncertainty.csv

Or for scatter charts using external CSV datasets:

type: scatter
data: 5-Data/datasets/countries.csv
fill: Density
xScale: log
yScale: log
labels: [Singapore]
r: 5
x:
  label: "Land Area (km²)"
y:
  label: "Population"
trending: true

Observable Plot Data Visualizations

Render rich data visualizations using Observable Plot (plot or observableplot). For further information: https://observablehq.github.io/plot/features/plots

Plot.plot({
  title: "For charts, an informative title",
  subtitle: "Subtitle to follow with additional context",
  caption: "Figure 1. A chart with a title, subtitle, and caption.",
  marks: [
    Plot.frame(),
    Plot.text(["Titles, subtitles, captions, and annotations assist interpretation by telling the reader what’s interesting. Don’t make the reader work to find what you already know."], {lineWidth: 30, frameAnchor: "middle"})
  ]
})

Plot.plot({
  title: "For charts, an informative title",
  subtitle: "Subtitle to follow with additional context",
  caption: "Figure 1. A chart with a title, subtitle, and caption.",
  marks: [
    Plot.frame(),
    Plot.text(["Titles, subtitles, captions, and annotations assist interpretation by telling the reader what’s interesting. Don’t make the reader work to find what you already know."], {lineWidth: 30, frameAnchor: "middle"})
  ]
})

1. Reading Time Frequency Histogram

Plot.rectY(
  [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15],
  Plot.binX(
    { y: "count" },
    { x: (d) => d, fill: "#3b82f6", tip: true, rx: 3 }
  )
)

2. 2026 Super El Niño (Godzilla El Niño)

Totally NOAA style! From data processing to the example, you can find the original one from https://observablehq.com/@fil/godzilla-el-nino

const sst = await fetch("https://climatereanalyzer.org/clim/sst_daily/json_2clim/oisst2.1_nino3.4_sst_day.json")
  .then((response) => response.json());

const yearly = sst.slice(0, -2);
const means = sst.filter((d) => d.name === "1991-2020")[0].data.slice(0, -1);
const stdev = d3
  .transpose(
    yearly
      .filter((d) => "1991" <= d.name && d.name <= "2020")
      .map((d) => d.data.slice(0, -1))
  )
  .map((d) => d3.deviation(d));

const means2 = d3.blur([...means], 15);
const stdev2 = d3.blur([...stdev], 15);

const data = yearly.flatMap((series) =>
  series.data
    .map((t, day) => {
      if (t === null || t === undefined) return null;
      return {
        day: day,
        name: series.name,
        year: series.name === "Preliminary" ? 2026 : +series.name,
        preliminary: series.name === "Preliminary",
        temperature: t,
        anomaly: t - means[day],
        deviation: stdev[day] ? (t - means[day]) / stdev[day] : null
      };
    })
    .filter(Boolean)
);

const last2026 = data.findLastIndex((d) => d.name === "2026");
if (last2026 !== -1) {
  data.splice(last2026 + 1, 0, {...data[last2026], name: "Preliminary", preliminary: true});
}

const point2026 = data.findLast((d) => d.name === "2026");

const date = day => new Date(Date.UTC(2000, 0, 1 + day));

Plot.plot({
  title: "Godzilla El Niño",
  subtitle: "The current Niño 3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly based on the 1991-2020 baseline",
  caption: "Figure 1. A good example of how Plot works.",
  width: 900,
  height: 540,
  marginRight: 40,
  x: {
    label: null,
    tickFormat: "%b",
    ticks: 12
  },
  y: {
    nice: 20
  },
  color: {
    scheme: "blues",
    unknown: "red"
  },
  marks: [
    d3.range(-3.5, 4.5, 0.5).map((d) =>
      Plot.line(stdev2, {
        x: (dev, i) => date(i),
        y: (dev, i) => means2[i] + dev * d,
        strokeWidth: d % 1 ? 0.25 : 0.5
      })
    ),
    Plot.line(data, {
      filter: (d) => d.name !== "Preliminary",
      x: (d) => date(d.day),
      y: "temperature",
      z: "name",
      stroke: (d) => (d.year === 2026 ? NaN : d.year),
      strokeWidth: (d) => (d.year === 2026 ? 2 : 0.5)
    }),
    Plot.line(data, {
      filter: (d) => d.name === "Preliminary",
      x: (d) => date(d.day),
      y: "temperature",
      z: "name",
      stroke: NaN,
      strokeWidth: 2,
      strokeDasharray: [2, 4]
    }),
    Plot.line(means, {
      x: (_, i) => date(i),
      y: Plot.identity,
      stroke: "orange",
      strokeWidth: 2
    }),
    Plot.axisY({tickSize: 15, dx: -5}),
    Plot.axisY([-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4], {
      y: (d) => means2[364] + d * stdev2[364],
      anchor: "right",
      tickSize: 0,
      tickFormat: (d) =>
        d === 0 ? "mean" : d === 1 ? `σ` : d === -1 ? `-σ` : `${d}σ`,
      label: "deviation"
    }),

    Plot.text(["2026"], {
      x: date(point2026.day),
      y: point2026.temperature,
      dx: 8,
      fill: "red",
      stroke: "white",
      strokeWidth: 2,
      fontWeight: "bold",
      textAnchor: "start"
    }),
    Plot.tip(
      data,
      Plot.pointer({
        x: (d) => date(d.day),
        y: "temperature",
        channels: {
          series: "name",
          date: (d) => date(d.day),
          temperature: "temperature",
          anomaly: "anomaly",
          deviation: "deviation"
        },
        format: {
          series: true,
          date: "%d %B",
          temperature: (d) => `${d}°C`,
          anomaly: (d) =>
            d < 0 ? `${d.toFixed(2)}°C` : `+${d.toFixed(2)}°C`,
          deviation: (d) =>
            d < 0 ? `${d.toFixed(2)}σ` : `+${d.toFixed(2)}σ`,
          x: false,
          y: false
        }
      })
    )
  ]
})

3. Rendering from Markdown Tables in the Same Note

You can use any Markdown table in the same note as the data source for Observable Plot or Chart DSL! Simply refer to id: #my-table-id or id: my-table-id:

Location Density Population Land area (km2) GDP
Monaco 19428 38857 2 7180
Singapore 8290 6110200 737 397000
Gibraltar (UK) 5800 39329 6.8 2400
Vatican City 2205 882 0.44 21
Bahrain 2034 1607049 790 44000
Maldives 1759 527799 298 5400
Malta 1686 539607 320 17800
Bangladesh 1333 173562364 130170 460000

^table-countries

Using Chart DSL (chart)

You can render a scatter chart referencing the table using our YAML-based Chart DSL:

type: scatter
id: table-countries
xScale: log
yScale: log
trending: true
fill: GDP
r: Density
x:
   label: "Land Area (km²)"
y:
   label: "Population"
markLines:
   - y: 10000000
     label: "10M Population Threshold"
     style: dashed
     color: "#f59e0b"
   - x: 1000
     label: "1,000 km² Threshold"
     style: dotted
     color: "#10b981"
width: 700px
Table-to-Data Column Resolution

When referencing a table, columns are resolved automatically:

  1. X and Y Dimensions: Matched first by matching your x and y labels, keys, or columns against table headers (with fuzzy matching for superscripts such as km² vs km2).
  2. Color Legend & Fill: Chosen from the remaining numeric columns in table order (numericCols.find((k) => k !== xCol && k !== yCol)). In the table above, Density appears before GDP, so points are colored by Density and the legend shows Density.
  3. Custom Fill Column: You can explicitly specify fill: or color: to pick any column (e.g. fill: GDP) for point colors and legend.
  4. 4D Bubble Chart (Size Mapping): Map another numeric dimension to point radius using r: or size: (e.g. r: GDP or r: Density):
type: scatter
id: table-countries
xScale: log
yScale: log
trending: true
fill: Density
r: GDP
x:
   label: "Land Area (km²)"
y:
   label: "Population"
markLines:
   - y: 10000000
     label: "10M Population Threshold"
     style: dashed
     color: "#f59e0b"
   - x: 1000
     label: "1,000 km² Threshold"
     style: dotted
     color: "#10b981"
width: 700px

Using Observable Plot (plot)

In Observable Plot code blocks, tables with hyphenated IDs (e.g. table-countries or ^table-countries) are preprocessed into accessible JavaScript identifiers (table_countries or table-countries directly):

Plot.plot({
  title: "Population vs. Land Area from Note Table",
  width: 700,
  height: 380,
  grid: true,
  x: { type: "log", label: "Land Area (km²) →" },
  y: { type: "log", label: "↑ Population" },
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(table_countries, {
      x: "Land area (km2)",
      y: "Population",
      fill: "Density",
      r: "GDP",
      tip: true
    }),
    Plot.text(table_countries, {
      x: "Land area (km2)",
      y: "Population",
      text: "Location",
      dy: -10,
      fontSize: 10
    })
  ]
})
